mnemonic.meaning: 観 observe + 察 inspect: watch and inspect closely.
mnemonic.reading: "KAN, SATSU!" (かんさつ) You watch the can until it's caught.

examples.ja: 子供たちは虫を観察した。
examples.en: The children observed the insects.

items.note: For careful, scientific watching: 観察日記 (observation diary).

mnemonic.meaning: KITSUI: a "KIT" so tight you can't zip it.

examples.ja: この靴は少しきつい。
examples.en: These shoes are a little tight.

items.note: Also for hard work and sharp words: 仕事がきつい, きつい言い方.

mnemonic.meaning: 袋 has 衣 (clothing) at the bottom: cloth made into a bag.
mnemonic.reading: "FUKU-ROW!" (ふくろ) A row of clothes (服) stuffed in a bag.

examples.ja: 袋はいりますか。
examples.en: Do you need a bag?

items.note: Used with 〜袋 as ぶくろ: 紙袋 (paper bag), 手袋 (gloves).

mnemonic.meaning: 偶 means chance, repeated: just by chance.
mnemonic.reading: "TAMA, TAMA!" (たまたま) A ball (玉) rolls your way by chance.

examples.ja: 駅で偶々友達に会った。
examples.en: I happened to meet a friend at the station.

items.note: Usually written in kana: たまたま.

mnemonic.meaning: 続 has 糸 (thread): a thread that goes on. What comes next.
mnemonic.reading: "TSU, ZUKI!" (つづき) The story continues; you love (好き) it.

examples.ja: 話の続きは明日にしよう。
examples.en: Let's leave the rest of the story for tomorrow.

items.note: Noun from 続く. 続きを読む = read on.

mnemonic.meaning: 騒 has 馬 (horse): horses stampeding. A big commotion.
mnemonic.reading: "SAWA-GI!" (さわぎ) A gaggle of geese makes a racket.

examples.ja: 外で何か騒ぎが起きている。
examples.en: Something's causing a commotion outside.

items.note: 騒ぐ = to make noise. 大騒ぎ = a big fuss.

mnemonic.meaning: 次 next + 第 order: what comes next depends on the order of things.
mnemonic.reading: "SHE, DIE!" (しだい) Whether she does depends on you.

examples.ja: 天気次第で予定を決めます。
examples.en: We'll decide the plan depending on the weather.

items.note: Noun + 次第 = depends on. V-stem + 次第 = as soon as: 着き次第 (as soon as I arrive).

mnemonic.meaning: 自 self + 慢 pride: proud of yourself. Bragging.
mnemonic.reading: "JEE, MAN!" (じまん) He shows off his muscles. Rhymes with 我慢 (Level 1).

examples.ja: 彼はいつも車を自慢している。
examples.en: He's always showing off his car.

items.note: Easy to mix up with 我慢 (がまん, endurance). 自慢の〜 = someone's pride and joy.

mnemonic.meaning: BUTSUKERU: the "you do it" partner of ぶつかる. You bang something into something.

examples.ja: 机に足をぶつけた。
examples.en: I banged my leg on the desk.

items.note: Also 気持ちをぶつける = to vent your feelings at someone.

mnemonic.meaning: 範 model + 囲 surround: a boundary drawn around something.
mnemonic.reading: "HAN, EE!" (はんい) Han Solo stays in range.

examples.ja: テストの範囲を教えてください。
examples.en: Please tell us what the test covers.

items.note: 範囲内 = within range. 試験範囲 = material covered on an exam.

mnemonic.meaning: 鉄 has 金 (metal): the metal you lose (失) if it rusts. Iron.
mnemonic.reading: "TETSU!" (てつ) The iron train (鉄道) rolls by.

examples.ja: 鉄は熱いうちに打て。
examples.en: Strike while the iron is hot.

items.note: 鉄道 (railway), 地下鉄 (subway).

mnemonic.meaning: 主 main + 張 stretch: stretching out your main point.
mnemonic.reading: "SHOE, CHOU!" (しゅちょう) He insists the shoe is his.

examples.ja: 彼は自分の意見を強く主張した。
examples.en: He strongly asserted his opinion.

items.note: Stating your view firmly. 自己主張 = asserting yourself.

mnemonic.meaning: 持 hold + 上 up: hold it and raise it.
mnemonic.reading: MOCHI (holding) + AGERU (raise): lift the mochi up. (もちあげる)

examples.ja: この箱は重くて持ち上げられない。
examples.en: This box is too heavy to lift.

items.note: Figuratively "to butter someone up".

mnemonic.meaning: 蹴 has 足 (foot): something you do with your foot.
mnemonic.reading: "KE-RU!" (ける) You kick the can down the road.

examples.ja: ボールを強く蹴った。
examples.en: I kicked the ball hard.

items.note: Also "to reject": 提案を蹴る (turn down a proposal). Godan despite ending in -eru.

mnemonic.meaning: 機 machine + 能 ability: what a machine is able to do.
mnemonic.reading: "KEE, NO!" (きのう) Same sound as 昨日 (yesterday). Yesterday the feature broke.

examples.ja: この携帯にはいろいろな機能がある。
examples.en: This phone has all sorts of features.

items.note: Same reading as 昨日 (yesterday). Context makes it clear.

mnemonic.meaning: 生 life + 物 thing: a thing with life.
mnemonic.reading: IKI (living) + MONO (thing): (いきもの)

examples.ja: 海にはたくさんの生き物がいる。
examples.en: There are many creatures in the sea.

items.note: Covers animals, insects, even plants loosely. 動物 is just animals.

mnemonic.meaning: 現 present + 状 condition: the present condition.
mnemonic.reading: "GEN, JOE!" (げんじょう) General Joe reports how things are now.

examples.ja: 現状を変えるのは難しい。
examples.en: It's hard to change the current situation.

items.note: Formal. 現状維持 = keeping the status quo.

mnemonic.meaning: 命 means order (and life): a command your life depends on.
mnemonic.reading: "MAY, JIRU!" (めいじる) May orders you to jump.

examples.ja: 社長は部下に調査を命じた。
examples.en: The president ordered his staff to investigate.

items.note: Formal. Everyday is 命令する or 言いつける. Also 命ずる.

mnemonic.meaning: SHABERU: "SHA-BE-RU!" The sound of someone who won't stop chatting.

examples.ja: 授業中にしゃべるな。
examples.en: Don't chatter in class.

items.note: Casual, often "talk a lot". Formal speaking is 話す.

mnemonic.meaning: ACHI (there) + KOCHI (here): over there and over here.

examples.ja: 鍵をあちこち探した。
examples.en: I searched all over for my keys.

items.note: Same as あちらこちら, more casual.

mnemonic.meaning: 掻 has 扌 (hand): fingers scratching.
mnemonic.reading: "KA-KU!" (かく) A cat scratches; same sound as 書く (write).

examples.ja: 蚊に刺されたところを掻いた。
examples.en: I scratched my mosquito bite.

items.note: Also in idioms: 汗をかく (to sweat), 恥をかく (to be embarrassed). Usually in kana.

mnemonic.meaning: 舞 dance + 台 platform: a platform for dancing.
mnemonic.reading: "BOO, TIE!" (ぶたい) The crowd boos the actor on stage.

examples.ja: 彼女は初めて舞台に立った。
examples.en: She stood on the stage for the first time.

items.note: Also the setting of a story: 物語の舞台.

mnemonic.meaning: 徐 slowly, repeated: slowly, slowly.
mnemonic.reading: "JOE JOE NI." (じょじょに) Little by little, Joe and Joe catch up.

examples.ja: 病気は徐々に良くなっている。
examples.en: The illness is gradually getting better.

items.note: Slightly formal. だんだん and 少しずつ are everyday.

mnemonic.meaning: 譲 has 言 (words): words saying "you go first".
mnemonic.reading: "YUZU-RU!" (ゆずる) You give your yuzu fruit to someone.

examples.ja: 電車でお年寄りに席を譲った。
examples.en: I gave my seat to an elderly person on the train.

items.note: 道を譲る = let someone pass. Also to sell or hand down.

mnemonic.meaning: 最 most + 中 middle: the very middle of it.
mnemonic.reading: "SIGH, CHUU!" (さいちゅう) You sigh in the middle of the meeting.

examples.ja: 食事の最中に電話が鳴った。
examples.en: The phone rang in the middle of dinner.

items.note: Grammar 〜の最中に is on the cheat sheet. Read もなか, it's a sweet.

mnemonic.meaning: 結 tie + 論 argument: tying up the argument.
mnemonic.reading: "KETSU, RON!" (けつろん) At the end, Ron reaches a conclusion.

examples.ja: まだ結論は出ていない。
examples.en: No conclusion has been reached yet.

items.note: 結論から言うと = to get to the point.

mnemonic.meaning: 代 substitute + 表 express: someone who speaks in place of others.
mnemonic.reading: "DIE, HYOU!" (だいひょう) The delegate rides a leopard (ひょう) into the meeting.

examples.ja: 彼女はクラスの代表に選ばれた。
examples.en: She was chosen as the class representative.

items.note: 日本代表 = the Japanese national team. 代表的 = typical.

mnemonic.meaning: 治 cure + 療 heal: curing and healing.
mnemonic.reading: "CHEE, RYOU!" (ちりょう) Cheese helps your dog Ryou heal.

examples.ja: 毎週病院で治療を受けている。
examples.en: I get treatment at the hospital every week.

items.note: For doctors and dentists. 治る is to recover; 治す is to cure.

mnemonic.meaning: HOTTO: the "ho" sound of a big sigh of relief.

examples.ja: 試験が終わってほっとした。
examples.en: I was relieved the exam was over.

items.note: Usually ほっとする. Different from ホット (hot).

mnemonic.meaning: 狂 has 犭 (beast): acting like a wild animal.
mnemonic.reading: "KURU-U!" (くるう) Crazy things keep coming (来る).

examples.ja: 時計が狂っている。
examples.en: The clock is off.

items.note: For people and machines: 予定が狂う (plans go wrong).
